summary: Reconciled .1R.2's unenumerated 'eight non-collapsible layers' claim against its concrete section-52/Matrix-E phase sequence, which bundles the mechanism-neutral HPAC verifier with B1/B7/N1/N2 production-authority repair in one 'Phase 2'. Re-derived from contracts (HPAC-001 section 18/section 19, RDGO-001 sections 6 and 10, PBRD-001 section 7), not assumed, that the verifier is architecturally separable from that repair: it consumes only the already independently-verified foundation (registry, presentation, proof, lifecycle stores), its HPAC-REQ-056 AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal output is contractually ephemeral and non-serializable (closing the anti-transfer/copied-result threat model by construction), and N2's repair is a consumer of the verifier rather than a co-requisite for building it. Produced a full implementation plan (verifier responsibilities/exclusions, input/output contracts, trust/provenance model, anti-transfer model, NON-REAL assurance classification, principal/proof/presentation/lifecycle consumption ownership, Gate-5/Gate-9 relationship, failure model, error-taxonomy reuse, persistence decision, 25-vector threat matrix, test plan, regression strategy) and froze the exact next two phase IDs following this repository's observed .<N>/.<N>.1 naming convention: 149O.20L.7O.3W.1R.2B.1R.1.1R.5 (verifier implementation) and ...1R.5.1 (its independent verification). No verifier code, no production trust-path file, no contract file was modified in this phase.
derived_correctness: The reconciliation was re-derived from primary sources, not taken on trust: the .1R.2 planning artifact was read in full (all 55 sections, including section 52's Matrix E table and section 54's stated rationale for bundling verifier+repair into 'Phase 2'), the six relevant contracts (RIHAC-001, RIASC-001, HPAC-001, PBRD-001, RDGO-001, RPAC-001) were read for their verifier-relevant normative text (HPAC-001 section 18's already-normative 8-step verifier algorithm, section 19's AuthenticatedHumanPrincipal contract), and the full .1R.1 through .1R.3.2.2.1 foundation-implementation chain was read to confirm which modules/types already exist in src/pcae/core/ (hpac_foundation.py, human_principal_registry.py, approval_presentation.py, human_authentication_proof.py, hpac_lifecycle.py, runtime_invocation_authority_consumption.py) versus what remains unbuilt (hpac_verifier.py does not exist; runtime_authority.py/runtime_dispatch_permission.py remain pre-verifier). The phase-ID naming convention (.<N> implementation / .<N>.1 verification / .<N>.2+ repair-and-reverify only if verification finds a blocking issue) was independently re-derived by listing docs/PHASE_149O_20L_7O_3W_1R* in chronological order and matching the observed .1R.3 to .1R.3.2.2.1 pattern, not assumed from the phase directive's own suggested numbering.
